content.thinking: I found the mismatch: scrape.yaml references the "metrics" port while the values file defines "http-metrics", so I need to fix scrape.yaml to match. I should also add a test verifying the two stay in sync, preferably with simple regex-based text parsing to avoid relying on PyYAML being installed.

Found the issue: `deploy/scrape.yaml` references the port name `metrics`, but `deploy/values-production.yaml` renamed it to `http-metrics`, with nothing validating the match. I'll fix the name mismatch and add a test to catch this going forward.

input.explanation:
The fault: in main, `deploy/scrape.yaml` (the ServiceMonitor) picks the endpoint to scrape by the port name `- port: metrics`. In main, `deploy/values-production.yaml` names that port `metrics.portName: http-metrics`, after the estate-wide rename to the platform convention. A ServiceMonitor port name that matches no port is not an error. Prometheus simply ends up with no targets, so no metrics came in and MetricsAbsent fired. Meanwhile the shop kept serving normally. The comment in `deploy/scrape.yaml` itself says "Nothing checks that the two agree", and that missing check is why the rename could break metrics silently. Rolling back the rename would only hide the problem until the convention was applied again.

The change:
- `deploy/scrape.yaml`: the endpoint's port is now `http-metrics`, matching `metrics.portName` in `deploy/values-production.yaml`. Path and interval are unchanged. The comment now names the test that keeps the two in step.
- `tests/io_shop/test_deploy_config.py` (new): reads both files from the repository root. It takes `portName` from the `metrics:` block of the values file and every `port:` from the ServiceMonitor's endpoints, and asserts that the metrics port name is among them. It uses plain text parsing, so it adds no YAML dependency. With the old `port: metrics` the test is written to fail. With this change it should pass, and it should catch any future rename of either side that isn't made to both.

Which revision these claims are about: everything above describes main. The running revision c3c36da3c66c07707f227b7e70b26813083061f3 is not in main's history, and I haven't read it. The investigation says it carried the `http-metrics` rename. Whether its copy of `scrape.yaml` still said `metrics` is the investigation's conclusion, not something I checked. That branch needs the same one-line scrape change before it is deployed again. No service source code is involved: nothing in the shop reads the port name.

# How the platform's Prometheus collects the shop's metrics.
#
# The ServiceMonitor the platform applies with the shop's chart, kept in the
# repository beside how the shop is deployed, so that how it is collected
# changes in the same pull request as what it is collected from.
#
# It selects the shop's Service by label, then the endpoint to scrape on that
# Service by the port's *name* - never its number - so a port can move without
# anything here being touched.
#
# The name here has to be the one `metrics.portName` in values-production.yaml
# gives the port. A name that matches no port is not an error to the operator,
# it is a target list with nothing in it - so
# tests/io_shop/test_deploy_config.py checks that the two agree.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: io-shop
  labels:
    release: prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: io-shop
  endpoints:
    - port: http-metrics
      path: /metrics
      interval: 15s

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

"""Whether the scrape config still finds the port the deployment names.

The ServiceMonitor selects the metrics endpoint by port *name*. A name that
matches no port is silently an empty target list, so metrics stop with no
error anywhere. This keeps deploy/scrape.yaml and
deploy/values-production.yaml in step.
"""

DEPLOY = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "deploy"


def _metrics_port_name() -> str:
    text = (DEPLOY / "values-production.yaml").read_text()
    block = re.search(r"^metrics:\s*\n((?:[ \t]+.*\n?|\s*\n)+)", text, re.MULTILINE)
    assert block, "values-production.yaml has no metrics: block"
    name = re.search(r"^\s+portName:\s*['\"]?([^'\"\s#]+)", block.group(1), re.MULTILINE)
    assert name, "metrics: block has no portName"
    return name.group(1)


def _scraped_port_names() -> list[str]:
    text = (DEPLOY / "scrape.yaml").read_text()
    _, _, endpoints = text.partition("endpoints:")
    return re.findall(r"^\s*-?\s*port:\s*['\"]?([^'\"\s#]+)", endpoints, re.MULTILINE)


def test_the_scrape_selects_the_port_name_the_deployment_gives_metrics() -> None:
    scraped = _scraped_port_names()

    assert scraped, "scrape.yaml selects no endpoint port"
    assert _metrics_port_name() in scraped

input.summary: Point the ServiceMonitor at the renamed http-metrics port and test that it matches metrics.portName
